# Canonical protocol vectors

## Session requests

The four digest values in `session-requests.tsv` are retained unchanged from
`dragginzgame/ic-auth` commit
`e52a40be75dd9809d0528189d84b43fe96952ad9`, file
`crates/ic-auth/tests/session_request.rs`, tests
`canonical_request_hash_preserves_exact_ttl_choice_and_scope_order` and
`absent_and_explicit_ttl_keep_independent_frozen_hashes`.
Source hashes are recorded in the repository's `reference.sha256`.

The TSV arrangement and surrounding tests are new. Expected values were retained
before implementing the replacement and are not generated by it. Their framing
is the literal ASCII domain `canic-application-session-request-v1` (no NUL),
big-endian u64 scope count, sorted scopes each prefixed by a big-endian u64 byte
length, and a single TTL tag: 0 for absent or 1 followed by big-endian u64 seconds.
The vectors are also checked with Perl `Digest::SHA` using that specification.

These establish unsigned request identity only. They are not signed credential,
Wire, proof-verification, session admission or storage qualification. The
historical domain string is retained for compatibility; there is no Canic
dependency. Original provenance and licensing remain at the repository root.

## Schema-2 claims

`claims-v2.hex` is the exact concatenation of the `VECTOR` string from
`crates/ic-auth/tests/portable.rs` at the same pinned commit. Its decoded length
is 250 bytes and SHA-256 is
`e0d179c866e21b8009fa5dba6bcf85ccc99065f83f141d9e9c2aeb2bc61a2e9d`.
The reference identifies this vector as assembled independently of its Rust
encoder. It was extracted before the replacement codec was written and checked
again using Perl `pack` and `Digest::SHA` against the documented field sequence.
No Python tooling or reference implementation was imported.

The fixture uses Ed25519 tag 1, network/application bytes `11`/`22` repeated
32 times, one-byte issuer/subject `01`/`02`, key/browser bytes `33`/`44`, slot 0,
generation 1, timestamps `0102030405060708`, `1112131415161718`,
`2122232425262728`, `3132333435363738`, nonce `55` repeated 16 times and one
`user` → `read` grant. All multibyte integers are big-endian. Counts and variable
byte lengths are u32; the schema is u16; generation/timestamps are u64. The
domain has its required trailing zero byte. The Certified vector differs only
at mechanism offset 30, where the signed tag is 0.

The deliberately inconsistent time window is accepted by the structural codec;
it cannot pass time validation. These fixtures do not establish proof validity,
browser caller binding, installed Wasm behavior or complete old/new interoperability.

## Ed25519 verification

`ed25519.tsv` retains the accepted public key, digest and signature from
`crates/ic-auth/tests/portable_signature.rs` at the same reference commit.
That source records independent Perl packing and OpenSSL signing, using the
public test-only seed `00..1f`. The exact source hash is in `reference.sha256`.

`../verify-ed25519-fixture.mjs` independently packs the schema-2 bytes and
reproduces the reference signature with Node/OpenSSL. It also computes the
SHA-256 key binding, standard SHA-224 self-authenticating browser caller and
wrong-message/noncanonical-scalar fixtures. Run:

```sh
node crates/ic-auth/tests/verify-ed25519-fixture.mjs
```

This vector uses the reference's raw browser bytes `44` repeated 32 times,
issuer/subject `01`/`02`, login window 10–100 ns, issuance/admission expiry 20–30
ns and `user` → `read`. The issuer signature is valid; the browser bytes serve
only the reference's caller-derivation contract and do not demonstrate an actual
SDK-generated login. No private production key or replacement Rust signer is used.
The extra all-zero-seed public key is another public test-only key, used to prove
that a different valid key cannot replace the enrolled key.

The `--print` mode emits independently computed candidate TSV bytes for deliberate
fixture review. Ordinary tests only read fixed expected bytes. This establishes
Ed25519/context acceptance, not session admission, issuer custody or certified/BLS
verification. Original provenance and licensing remain at the repository root.

## Root-delegation signing commitments

`delegation.tsv` retains the batch-header, issuer-leaf and derivation-path hashes
from `crates/ic-auth/tests/canonical.rs` at the same pinned reference commit.
The fixture's identities, `test_key_1` name, domains, labels and field values are
protocol test data, not runtime trust anchors. Reference files are recorded in
`reference.sha256`.

The certificate bytes, certificate digest and issuer-binding digest are separately
assembled from that reference fixture using Node buffers and OpenSSL SHA-256 in
`../verify-delegation-fixtures.mjs`. The script checks all six records and first
asserts the three retained reference hashes. It imports no replacement code.
Run `node crates/ic-auth/tests/verify-delegation-fixtures.mjs` from the repository
root. Rust tests consume the frozen TSV, never the replacement encoder's output
as their expected bytes.

The new domain records factor the common issuer authorization fields into one
passive value; their Rust shape is not a Wire-layout change. Certificate issuance
time contributes to the certificate digest but is absent from the issuer leaf.
Bounds and strict grant ordering are structural admission only; these vectors
prove no root signature, grant authority, enrollment or session admission.

## Volatile receiver sequences

`memory.tsv` extends the public Ed25519 test seed with nine independently packed
schema-2 credentials. `../verify-memory-fixtures.mjs` uses Node/OpenSSL to verify
all bytes and signatures; its initial case must equal the retained `ed25519.tsv`
reference. Renewal preserves the browser/account/slot/generation and 10–100 ns
login window. Replacement uses a different browser and higher slot generation;
other cases test rebinding refusal and a fresh old-generation credential after
replay pruning. The future case uses a different subject, login 110–200 ns and
proof 120–130 ns, demonstrating that temporary unknown denial through 101 ns
cannot conclusively revoke unseen future credentials. `other-device` adds slot 1
for the original issuer/subject; `other-issuer` keeps subject `02` and slot 0 but
binds issuer `03`. Their distinct browser keys and nonces test independent device
fences and issuer-qualified quotas without altering any earlier fixture bytes.
Both issuers use the public fixture signing key under separate protected enrollment
identities. These are new semantic
test sequences, not copied legacy engine
code or actual SDK browser logins. See the
[memory receiver boundary](../../../../docs/development/memory-receiver-boundary.md)
for the qualified operations and remaining host/recovery scope.
